tells.1: Upbeat padding that softens the news ('Quick heads-up', 'On a happier note', 'so you have more ways to fit a workout into your week', 'we'll be glad to help'), which reads like scripted positivity added around a price increase
tells.2: Stiff, templated phrasing ('will increase', 'will take effect for you') and the generic benefit line 'to give you more options during the week', which is slightly illogical for a Sunday addition; the curly apostrophes also suggest pasted output
tells.4: Mild formulaic redundancy ('when the $135 rate takes effect for you'), but otherwise little to flag

reason: Version 3 states the increase, the grandfathering for current members and the new classes in the fewest words, with no spin, so it reads as direct and credible. Version 4 is a close second, while 1 over-sweetens the news and 2 sounds corporate.
